deliverables.acceptance: Questions identify authority, critical assets, licensing, normal administration, response owners and budget.
Twelve named security/reliability/operations requirements include concrete validation methods.
Source boundaries distinguish subscription activity, owned guest Syslog and local synthetic formats.
Logical data/control paths and management/authentication/storage responsibilities are explicit.
Five exercise roles have RACI ownership for onboarding, engineering, investigation, cost and handover.
Per-source ownership, acceptance gaps and reusable onboarding criteria are documented.
Twelve IDs map to source, severity, schedule, investigation limits and disabled state.
API technique/tactic labels, unmapped areas and current-taxonomy uncertainty remain explicit.
Machine-readable coverage matches all twelve versioned definitions and links queries/runbooks.
Triage, investigation, escalation, closure, tuning and platform failure procedures are actionable.
Evidence class, lineage, identity/scope, health uncertainty, impact and owner are assessed in order.
Response recommendations require explicit authority and evidence-backed classification.
Health definitions separate quiet event sources, stopped machines, stale snapshots and unavailable measurement.
Existing workspace controls, payload/billable distinction, billing lag and finite cost review are explicit.
Metric formulas, denominator/time scopes, unknowns and noncontractual exercise targets are defined.
Changes require scope, hashes, tests, approval, protected exact-head CI and actual read-back.
Source-to-case diagnostic sequence, role-based routes and eight realistic ticket exercises exist.
Customer acceptance distinguishes implemented artifacts, actual cloud proof and unexecuted live gates.
Twelve risks have concrete controls, owners and residual acceptance decisions.
Successor checks, recovery boundaries, private-state handling and operator-led closure are documented.

live_incident_gate.reason: This offline customer package cannot establish cloud acceptance alone. The global final status now links the actual isolated Sentinel lifecycle; synthetic tickets still describe fictional service scenarios, not that real laboratory incident.
